key_insight: Apparent learning gains in an Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration agent largely disappeared after controlling for shared references, with no statistically distinguishable benefit from memory or policy adaptation.
engineering_relevance: Migration agents need leakage-resistant evaluation and behavioral validation against Oracle, not just PostgreSQL acceptance or reference similarity.
method: Compare persistent memory and policy adaptation with no-memory and model-free copying baselines.
Audit shared references and rerun evaluation with reference-grouped splits.
Test real PL/SQL behavior, human-gated fixes, and retrieval stability as memory grows.
evidence_signal: Across 1,833 documentation-derived pairs, 72% of held-out units shared training references; a grouped rerun found a memory effect of 0.005 [-0.003, 0.017], while 10–22% of PostgreSQL-accepted real PL/SQL units were behaviorally incorrect.
watch_item: Scaling memory can weaken retrieval: the reported retrieval margin declined 54% as the knowledge base grew from 12 to 1,200 entries.
paper_title: Does a Self-Learning Migration Agent Learn? An Audited Evaluation of Evidence-Graded Experience Memory for Oracle-to-PostgreSQL Migration
